headline: High: Windsurf’s default filesystem/MCP/tooling can conflict with Pathway’s document-processing outputs, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pathway is a document-processing agent with no direct shared channel, but Windsurf reads workspace files, uses clipboard, and can call MCP servers. If Pathway outputs are placed in shared files or copied into Windsurf, Windsurf may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. The pathway is plausible in default workflows, though not proven by direct pair evidence.
conditions: IF Pathway outputs are written into a workspace file that Windsurf opens
IF content from Pathway is pasted into Windsurf via clipboard
IF Windsurf is configured to follow instructions found in file content
mitigations: Keep Pathway outputs in a separate directory
Disable auto-open of generated documents in Windsurf
Use a strict prompt delimiter for any copied text
Review file content before pasting into Windsurf
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for generated artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pathway has no filesystem read/write or network egress, while Windsurf can read workspace files, use MCP, and has broad network egress. If sensitive files are shared in the workspace, Windsurf can ingest them and transmit context to external services. Pathway itself does not appear to exfiltrate, so the main leakage path is from shared files into Windsurf.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are present in Windsurf’s workspace
IF Windsurf sends workspace context to its model proxy or MCP servers
IF Pathway outputs are stored alongside sensitive files
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Restrict Windsurf to a minimal project folder
Disable or limit MCP servers for sensitive sessions
Remove secrets from files before opening them
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pathway cannot write files or modify git, but Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and supports shared state via local filesystem across instances. That creates a real conflict surface if both operate on the same workspace or repo, even though Pathway itself lacks write authority. Uncertainty is limited because Windsurf’s write capabilities are explicit.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or repository
IF Windsurf auto-executes edits while Pathway is generating artifacts
IF multiple Windsurf instances share the same local filesystem state
mitigations: Use separate working directories per agent
Pause Windsurf before Pathway writes outputs
Avoid concurrent edits to the same git branch
Check in changes only after manual review
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pathway can generate document outputs that Windsurf may consume as workspace content or follow-up context. Windsurf’s agentic loop and tool use mean it may act on those outputs without independent verification unless the operator intervenes. This is a plausible default workflow risk, though not directly evidenced for this exact pair.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses Pathway-produced text as authoritative input
IF Windsurf auto-executes or approves actions based on generated content
IF no human verification step is inserted between agents
mitigations: Require manual review of Pathway outputs before actioning
Use a checklist for any generated facts or code
Disable auto-execute for sensitive workflows
Keep Pathway outputs read-only until verified
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in the profiles. Pathway is open-source and non-networked, while Windsurf is a closed-source IDE with broad egress and model-proxy/MCP use, so compliance risk exists only if regulated data is placed into Windsurf. The other agent is not cited because no separate compliance regime is stated for Pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is opened inside Windsurf
IF Windsurf routes that data to external model services
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not documented here
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in Windsurf sessions
Use redacted copies for review
Confirm vendor retention settings before use
Segregate compliance-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: obtain vendor compliance attestations
